summary: This article explains how traditional craftsmen hammer and engrave copper and brass by hand into coffee pots, trays, and decorative items.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Metalwork: Shaping Copper and Brass”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: a skilled worker who makes things by hand, often beautifully
to heat metal so that it becomes soft and easier to shape
a place where people make or repair things by hand

challengeTerms.def: a material made by combining two or more metals
a metalworking technique that presses a design into a surface by pushing the metal from the front, without cutting any away
made to look decorative or beautiful, rather than only useful

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that a handmade object made with great skill is more special than a quick, machine-made one? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how an artisan turns a flat sheet of metal into a finished, decorated item.
struggling: Pre-teach artisan, anneal, and workshop with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use alloy, chasing, and ornamental in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
